title: Relay message model v2
description: The canonical wire contract for Relay's message model: one send is one message, message content is immutable, every stored part carries a permanent identity, a reply is a pointer rather than a copied quote, and a reaction is one emoji per actor per slot. Relay-Server owns this file. Every shape here is generated from and validated against real server responses by server/scripts/contract-fixtures-test.ts; nothing may be added to it that the server does not emit.
$comment: Clients MUST tolerate part types they do not know. The Part union is deliberately open: an unrecognised `type` matches $defs/UnknownPart, which requires only the identity fields (part_id, part_index) and permits any other member. Render such a part with the message's fallback_text and leave it otherwise untouched — do not drop it, and do not fail the message. Clients MUST also tolerate additive members on known shapes: Relay adds optional fields without a version bump.

messageId.description: A client-generated message identity. Lowercase Crockford base32 ULID; the client mints it before queueing the send and it is both the canonical id and the send's only idempotency mechanism. A retry with the same id replays the stored message; another sender's use of the id is a 409.

partId.description: A permanent part identity, assigned at commit. A reply or a reaction that targets one exact part names it by this.

Actor.description: Anyone who can act in a conversation. Humans are `user`, agents are `agent`; storage and wire spell it the same way, and there is no `system` actor — a group notice is sent by the person who caused it.

mentionHandle.description: The handle of a mentioned user or agent, without the leading '@'.

mentions.description: The handles this message mentions, each of which must be written as '@handle' in the part's `text` — at its start or after a space, newline, bracket or quote. A handle typed but never confirmed against the sender's suggestion list is absent here and stays plain text. There are no offsets: a mention can only ever be the handle itself.

StyleRange.description: One formatting run over a text part, in the same UTF-16 offsets mentions use. Presentation only: the text stays canonical and fallback text ignores styling.

styles.description: An empty array is meaningful: it marks structured plain text, distinguishing it from a legacy Markdown body. Absent means legacy.

blurHash.description: Compact placeholder a client decodes into a soft preview before the bytes download.

MediaPart.description: A photo, video, audio file or document. Attachment-backed media carries `attachment_id` and a capability `url`; remote media carries `url` alone.

LinkPreviewPart.description: Metadata the SENDER resolved, carried with the message, so a recipient never opens a connection to a URL somebody else chose. `title` and `description` are stored with the part and echoed on history reads; they are absent from the send response and from event payloads, so a client that needs them reads them back.

DataPart.description: A structured component. `data.type` names the component. A group notice carries its GroupMutationData here; see group-lifecycle-event.schema.json.

UnknownPart.description: The catch-all that keeps the Part union open. A client that meets a part type it does not know MUST render the message's fallback_text for it rather than dropping the part or rejecting the message.

Part.description: One part of a message, discriminated on `type`. The union is open by design; see UnknownPart.

oneOf.description: A pointer, never a copy. The client draws the quote from the target message it already has; Relay stores no snapshot, so there is no quote to go stale and no quote state to interpret. A target the reader cannot see is a pointer that resolves to nothing — render the reply without a quote.

part_id.description: Present when the reply targeted one specific part.

Reaction.description: One reaction as projected onto a message. One per (message, target slot, actor): adding a second emoji to the same slot replaces the first, and removing one that is not there is a no-op.

target_part_id.description: The part this reaction targets; null for a whole-message reaction.

Message.description: One stored message as one viewer sees it. Content is immutable — there is no edit, no unsend, no version and no tombstone — so this is the row plus its parts, its reactions on a read, and (in a direct conversation) its receipt stamps.

kind.description: `notice` is a group notice ("Alice added Bob"), sent by the person who did it rather than by a system participant. Its part 0 is the human-readable line and part 1 is a `data` part carrying the structured mutation.

is_from_me.description: True when the authenticated account this payload was projected for is the sender. Relay resolves direction so a client never compares sender.id against its own identity — a comparison that is wrong for every other human in a group.

reactions.description: Resolved on reads. A send response and an event payload carry the committed message alone and omit this.

fallback_text.description: A plain-text rendering of the whole message, for notifications, previews and any client that cannot render a part it was handed.

status.description: Direct conversations carry one stamp per message; a group message is always `sent`, the way iMessage behaves in groups.

VisibleMessage.description: Retained name for the one message shape. Unsend is gone, so there is nothing invisible to distinguish it from.

IncomingPart.description: A part as a client submits it. The server mints the identity; a client never supplies part_id or part_index.

SendRequestV2.description: POST /v2/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages. One send is one message: mixed media and text stay together instead of being split into a run of messages. `message_id` is the whole idempotency story — retrying the same id replays the original 201, and no Idempotency-Key header is involved.

reply_to.description: A pointer to a message of this conversation, optionally to one exact part of it.

invoked_agent_ids.description: DEPRECATED and ignored. An agent is a normal group member now; shipped SDKs still send this, so the field is accepted rather than rejected. New clients must omit it.

invocation_id.description: DEPRECATED and ignored, for the same reason as invoked_agent_ids.

SendResponseV2.$comment: 201. A retry with the same message_id replays this exact body.

SendResponseV1.description: 201 from POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages. The array always has exactly one element: Relay no longer splits a send. Shipped clients read an array, which is the only reason it is still one.

ReactionRequest.description: POST /v1/messages/{message_id}/reactions. Omit target_part_id to react to the whole message. Repeating a request changes nothing the second time, so there is no operation id.

target_part_id.description: One exact part of the target message. Null or absent means the whole message.

ReactionResult.description: Both the 200 body and the reaction.changed / reaction.added / reaction.removed event payload.

changed.description: False when the request was a no-op — removing a reaction that was not there, or re-adding the one already in the slot. Events are emitted only when this is true.

Receipt.description: The 200 body of POST /v1/conversations/{id}/read and /delivered: the watermark this actor advanced to. `read` implies delivered; an older or repeated target changes nothing.

advanced.description: False when the watermark was already at or past the named message.

HistoryPage.description: GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages, newest first, inside the caller's membership window.
